note.explanation: Biology is the study of life. It has many branches because living things can be studied in different ways: by their structure, functions, development, relationships, and classification. Scientists use observations, hypotheses, deductions, and experiments to investigate questions.
examples: Physiology studies the functions of living organisms and their parts.
note.simple: Biology studies living things. Its branches help us focus on one kind of question at a time. The scientific method is a careful way to test possible answers.
note.checkQuestion: Which branch studies the functions of living organisms and their parts?
note.title: Branches of Biology and the Scientific Method
steps: Form a hypothesis that could explain it.
Analyse the results and decide whether the hypothesis is supported.
note.answer: Biology is the study of life, and the scientific method uses observations, hypotheses, deductions, and experiments to investigate biological questions.

mcqs.stem: Q1.1. Which branch of Biology focuses on the study of the structure and function of cells?
rationales: Cytology studies cells, including their structure and functions.
Microbiology studies microscopic organisms, not specifically the structure and function of cells.
Histology studies tissues.
Ecology studies relationships between organisms and their environment.

mcqs.stem: Q1.2. The study of the processes of heredity and variation in living organisms is known as:
rationales: Ecology studies organisms and their environment.
Genetics studies heredity and variation in living organisms.
Anatomy studies the structure of organisms.
Embryology studies development of an organism from fertilization.

mcqs.stem: Q1.3. Insulin made through bacteria is an example of the technique of:
rationales: Parasitology studies parasites and their relationships with hosts.
Biotechnology uses organisms or biological processes to make useful products such as insulin.
Biochemistry studies chemical processes in living organisms.
Histology studies tissues.

mcqs.stem: Q1.4. Heart pumps blood, stomach digests food, and kidneys excrete wastes. The statement comes from.
rationales: Physiology is concerned with functions such as pumping blood, digesting food, and excreting wastes.
Anatomy studies the structure of body parts rather than what they do.
Morphology studies the form and external features of organisms.
Histology studies tissues.

mcqs.stem: Q1.5. Which branch of Biology involves the study of the classification of organisms?
rationales: Taxonomy deals with the identification, naming, and classification of organisms.
Physiology studies the functions of organisms and their parts.
Palaeontology studies fossils.
Biogeography studies the geographical distribution of organisms.

mcqs.stem: Q1.6. Which step comes between making hypothesis and doing experiments?
rationales: Deductions are made from a hypothesis before they are tested by experiments.
Observations are used to identify a problem and usually come before forming a hypothesis.
Summarizing results comes after experiments have been performed.
Analysing data follows the collection of experimental results.

mcqs.stem: Q1.7. Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the scientific method?
rationales: The scientific method relies on evidence.
Formulating hypotheses is a part of scientific investigation.
A hypothesis is a proposed explanation and may be rejected or changed after testing.
Scientific ideas are tested carefully and rigorously.

mcqs.stem: Q1.8. Choose the correct sequence of steps of scientific method?
rationales: The sequence starts with observations, then a hypothesis, deductions, and experiments.
A law and theory are not the next steps in the basic investigation sequence given here.
Observations normally lead to the hypothesis, rather than the hypothesis preceding observations.
This sequence begins with established ideas and places observations last, so it is not the scientific-method sequence.

(c) Mosquitoes cannot tolerate smoke and are repelled
mcqs.stem: Q1.9. People who slept near smoky fire had less chance to suffer from malaria. Why?
rationales: Smoke around a fire does not kill *Plasmodium* already present in a person's blood.
The explanation is not that increased air temperature kills *Plasmodium* in the air.
Smoke repels mosquitoes, reducing the chance of mosquito bites and malaria transmission.
Smoke does not directly kill *Plasmodium* inside mosquitoes in the way described.

options: (b) Disproves many hypotheses and gets some hypothesis proved
(c) Is sure that he will prove the hypotheses
(d) Gets a chance to work in the laboratory
mcqs.stem: Q1.10. Experiments are very important in scientific method because a researcher
rationales: Experiments do not guarantee that every result will be correct.
Testing can disprove many hypotheses and provide evidence supporting some hypotheses.
A researcher cannot be sure in advance that a hypothesis will be proved.
The purpose of experiments is to test ideas, not simply to provide laboratory work.

written.text: Q1.1. Define the following branches of Biology. Genetics, Anatomy, Palaeontology, Marine Biology, Pathology
written.finalAnswer: Genetics: the study of heredity and variation. Anatomy: the study of the internal structure of organisms. Palaeontology: the study of fossils. Marine Biology: the study of organisms living in the sea. Pathology: the study of diseases.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the subject studied by Genetics.
rubric.how: State that Genetics studies heredity and variation.

rubric.why: Anatomy is identified by the structure it studies.
rubric.how: State that Anatomy studies internal structure.

rubric.why: Fossils are the key subject of Palaeontology.
rubric.how: State that Palaeontology studies fossils.

rubric.why: The definition must identify organisms in the marine environment.
rubric.how: State that Marine Biology studies organisms living in the sea.

rubric.why: Diseases are the subject studied by Pathology.
rubric.how: State that Pathology studies diseases.

modelAnswer: Genetics is the study of heredity and variation.
Anatomy is the study of the internal structure of organisms.
Palaeontology is the study of fossils.
Marine Biology is the study of organisms living in the sea.
Pathology is the study of diseases.

written.text: Q1.2. Which branch of Biology involves the study of the development of organisms from fertilization to birth or hatching?

rubric.why: The answer should connect the branch with development starting at fertilization.
rubric.how: Name the branch that studies development from fertilization.

rubric.why: The correct branch name is needed for the final mark.
rubric.how: Write Embryology.

modelAnswer: The branch that studies the development of organisms from fertilization to birth or hatching is Embryology.

written.text: Q1.3. How is the profession of medicine and surgery different from animal husbandry?
written.finalAnswer: Medicine and surgery deal with the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of diseases in humans; animal husbandry deals with the care, breeding, and management of livestock for useful products.

rubric.why: The answer must distinguish the human-health focus of medicine and surgery.
rubric.how: Mention diagnosis or treatment of diseases in humans.

rubric.why: The answer must identify animal husbandry as the care and management of animals.
rubric.how: Mention care, breeding, or management of livestock.

modelAnswer: Medicine and surgery deal with the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of diseases in humans.
Animal husbandry deals with the care, breeding, and management of livestock for useful products.

written.text: Q1.4. Differentiate between Morphology and Physiology
written.finalAnswer: Morphology studies the form and external features of organisms, whereas Physiology studies the functions of organisms and their parts.

rubric.why: A valid difference must state what Morphology examines.
rubric.how: Connect Morphology with form or external features.

rubric.why: The contrasting focus of Physiology completes the comparison.
rubric.how: Connect Physiology with functions of organisms or their parts.

modelAnswer: Morphology studies the form and external features of organisms.
Physiology studies the functions of organisms and their parts.

written.finalAnswer: Computational Biology is the use of computers, mathematical tools, and statistical methods to collect, store, analyse, and interpret biological data.

rubric.why: The definition must connect computer methods with biological work.
rubric.how: Mention using computers to work with biological information.

rubric.why: The purpose of those tools is to process or interpret biological data.
rubric.description: State what is done with the data.
rubric.how: Mention analysing, storing, or interpreting biological data.

modelAnswer: Computational Biology uses computers and mathematical or statistical tools to collect, store, analyse, and interpret biological data.

written.text: Q1.6. What is the role of observation and experimentation in the scientific method?
written.finalAnswer: Observation helps a scientist notice a problem, collect information, and form a hypothesis. Experimentation tests deductions made from the hypothesis and provides evidence to support, reject, or modify it.

rubric.why: Observation provides the starting information for scientific investigation.
rubric.how: Say that observation helps identify a problem or collect information.

rubric.why: Experiments test the proposed explanation and provide evidence.
rubric.how: Say that experiments test deductions or a hypothesis.

modelAnswer: Observation helps a scientist notice a problem and collect information for forming a hypothesis.
Experimentation tests deductions made from the hypothesis and provides evidence to support, reject, or modify it.

written.text: Q1.1. Link the study of Biology with that of Physics, Chemistry, Statistics, Geography, Economics and Computer Science.
written.finalAnswer: Biology links with Physics through biophysics, with Chemistry through biochemistry, with Statistics through the analysis of biological data, with Geography through the distribution of organisms, with Economics through the economic value and management of biological resources, and with Computer Science through computational biology.

rubric.why: This shows the connection between biological processes and physical principles.
rubric.how: Give biophysics or a valid physical application in Biology.

rubric.why: Biochemistry is the direct link between Biology and Chemistry.
rubric.how: Name biochemistry or describe chemical processes in organisms.

rubric.why: Statistics helps analyse biological observations and results.
rubric.how: Explain that statistical methods analyse biological data.

rubric.why: Geography helps study where organisms occur and how place relates to living things.
rubric.how: Mention distribution of organisms or their geographical environment.

rubric.why: Examples of the remaining links show how Biology combines with other fields.
rubric.description: Link Biology with Economics and Computer Science.
rubric.how: Mention biological resources or computational analysis of biological data.

modelAnswer: Biology links with Physics through biophysics, which applies physical principles to living systems.
Biology links with Chemistry through biochemistry, the study of chemical processes in living organisms.
Statistics helps biologists organise and analyse observations and experimental data.
Geography is linked with Biology through the study of the distribution of organisms in different regions and environments.
Economics is linked with Biology through the use and management of biological resources.
Computer Science is linked with Biology through computational biology, which uses computers to analyse biological data.

written.text: Q1.2. Explain how the study of Biology can lead to different professional studies.
written.finalAnswer: The study of Biology can lead to professions and further studies in medicine and surgery, animal husbandry, agriculture, forestry, fisheries, biotechnology, and other fields concerned with living organisms and their products.

rubric.why: The answer must connect biological knowledge with professional pathways.
rubric.description: Introduce the link between Biology and professions.
rubric.how: State that biological study prepares people for careers involving living things.

rubric.why: Medicine and surgery are major professional fields based on Biology.
rubric.how: Name medicine or surgery and connect it with human health.

rubric.why: Applied biological professions include managing animals and crops.
rubric.how: Name animal husbandry, agriculture, or a related field.

rubric.why: Another valid professional study demonstrates the breadth of Biology careers.
rubric.how: Name biotechnology, fisheries, forestry, or another valid field.

modelAnswer: Biology provides knowledge of living organisms and their functions, which prepares students for many professional studies.
Knowledge of the human body and diseases can lead to medicine and surgery.
Knowledge of animals and plants can lead to animal husbandry, agriculture, forestry, and fisheries.
Biological knowledge can also lead to biotechnology and other professions that use living organisms or their products.

written.text: Q1.3. Science is a collaborative field in which scientists work together to share knowledge. Prove this statement by giving examples.
written.finalAnswer: Science is collaborative because scientists share observations and results, build on one another's findings, and test ideas together. For example, scientists investigating malaria contributed different discoveries about the parasite and its transmission, while other scientists tested and extended this work.

rubric.why: Sharing information is the central idea in the question.
rubric.how: Mention sharing observations, results, or knowledge.

rubric.why: Science progresses when later researchers use earlier findings.
rubric.how: Say that scientists build on or test one another's work.

rubric.why: A relevant chapter example is needed to support the statement.
rubric.how: Use the investigations into malaria as an example.

rubric.why: The example must show different contributions to understanding the problem.
rubric.how: Mention discoveries about the malaria parasite or mosquito transmission.

modelAnswer: Science is collaborative because scientists communicate their observations and results and share their knowledge.
Scientists build on earlier discoveries, repeat investigations, and test or extend the ideas of other researchers.
The discovery of the cause and transmission of malaria is an example: different scientists investigated the parasite and the role of mosquitoes.
Their combined findings helped develop a fuller explanation of malaria than one scientist's work alone could provide.

written.text: Q1.4. How a hypothesis is converted to theory, law and principle?
written.finalAnswer: A hypothesis is tested by deductions and experiments. If repeated tests support it, it may be accepted as a theory. A theory that is repeatedly verified and expresses a consistent natural relationship may be stated as a law. A principle is a well-established general truth or fundamental rule supported by evidence.

rubric.why: Testing is necessary before a hypothesis can gain wider acceptance.
rubric.description: Explain how a hypothesis is tested.
rubric.how: Mention deductions, experiments, or repeated testing.

rubric.why: A theory is supported by repeated testing and evidence.
rubric.description: Explain the move from hypothesis to theory.
rubric.how: State that repeatedly supported hypotheses may be accepted as theories.

rubric.why: The answer must distinguish a law as a repeatedly verified relationship or regularity.
rubric.description: Explain the place of a law.
rubric.how: Connect a law with repeated verification and a consistent natural relationship.

rubric.why: The definition of principle completes the requested account.
rubric.how: Describe a principle as an established general truth or fundamental rule.

modelAnswer: A hypothesis is tested by making deductions and performing experiments.
When a hypothesis is repeatedly supported by evidence, it may be accepted as a theory.
A repeatedly verified theory that expresses a consistent natural relationship may be stated as a law.
A principle is a well-established general truth or fundamental rule supported by evidence.

written.text: Q1.5. What are the basic steps a scientist adopts in order to solve a scientific problem?
written.finalAnswer: The basic steps are observations, hypothesis, deductions, experiments, and analysis of results. The results are used to accept, reject, or modify the hypothesis.

rubric.why: Investigation begins with observations that reveal a problem.
rubric.how: Begin with observation of a problem or phenomenon.

rubric.why: The scientist proposes an explanation and derives testable consequences.
rubric.description: State the hypothesis and deduction steps.
rubric.how: Write hypothesis followed by deductions.

rubric.why: Experiments test deductions from the hypothesis.
rubric.how: Mention performing experiments to test the deductions.

rubric.why: The investigation must end by considering evidence and the status of the hypothesis.
rubric.how: Analyse results and accept, reject, or modify the hypothesis.

modelAnswer: Observe a problem or phenomenon and collect relevant information.
Form a hypothesis to explain the observations.
Make deductions from the hypothesis.
Perform experiments to test the deductions.
Analyse the results and use the evidence to accept, reject, or modify the hypothesis.

written.text: Q1.6. Describe the work of different scientists in discovering the cause of malaria.
written.finalAnswer: Laveran observed the malaria parasite in the blood of patients. Manson proposed that mosquitoes might transmit malaria. Ross investigated mosquitoes and showed that they could carry the malaria parasite and transmit infection. These contributions established the role of mosquitoes in the spread of malaria.

rubric.why: Laveran's observation identified the parasite in malaria patients.
rubric.how: State that Laveran observed the parasite in patients' blood.

rubric.why: Manson's suggestion connected mosquitoes with malaria transmission.
rubric.how: State that Manson proposed a mosquito role in transmission.

rubric.why: Ross's work experimentally investigated mosquitoes as carriers.
rubric.how: Name Ross and describe his mosquito investigations.

rubric.why: The answer must explain the result linking mosquitoes with infection.
rubric.how: Explain that mosquitoes carry and transmit the parasite.

rubric.why: The conclusion connects the scientists' work to understanding the cause and spread of malaria.
rubric.how: Conclude that mosquitoes play a role in spreading malaria.

modelAnswer: Laveran observed the malaria parasite in the blood of patients suffering from malaria.
Manson proposed that mosquitoes might be involved in transmitting malaria.
Ross investigated mosquitoes and their relationship with the malaria parasite.
His work showed that mosquitoes could carry the parasite and transmit infection.
Together, these findings established the role of mosquitoes in the spread of malaria.

written.text: Q1.7. Write a descriptive note on the experiments performed by Ross.
written.finalAnswer: Ross studied malaria transmission using birds and mosquitoes. He allowed mosquitoes to feed on infected birds and then examined them, finding parasite development in the mosquitoes. He then allowed the infected mosquitoes to bite healthy birds, which developed malaria. The experiments supported the conclusion that mosquitoes transmit malaria.

rubric.why: The organisms used in the experiments must be identified.
rubric.how: Mention birds and mosquitoes.

rubric.why: The first stage exposed mosquitoes to infection.
rubric.how: State that mosquitoes fed on infected birds.

rubric.why: The observation in mosquitoes is a key experimental result.
rubric.description: State what Ross observed in mosquitoes.
rubric.how: Mention parasite development or presence in the mosquitoes.

rubric.why: The next stage tested whether mosquitoes could pass infection on.
rubric.how: State that mosquitoes exposed healthy birds to infection by biting them.

rubric.why: The conclusion must follow from the experimental result.
rubric.how: Conclude that mosquitoes transmit malaria.

modelAnswer: Ross investigated the transmission of malaria using birds and mosquitoes.
He allowed mosquitoes to feed on birds infected with malaria.
He examined the mosquitoes and observed that the parasite developed in them.
He then allowed these mosquitoes to bite healthy birds.
The healthy birds developed malaria, supporting the conclusion that mosquitoes transmit the disease.

written.text: Q1.1. Why is it important to classify biology into different branches such as botany, zoology, and microbiology? How does specialization benefit scientific research?
written.finalAnswer: Biology covers an enormous variety of organisms and processes, so dividing it into branches makes its study organised and manageable. Specialization allows researchers to develop detailed knowledge and suitable methods for a focused field, while sharing results with other branches helps solve larger biological problems.

rubric.why: The answer should explain why Biology is divided into branches.
rubric.how: Say that branches organise the large subject and its variety of life.

rubric.why: Examples show how branches focus on particular groups of organisms.
rubric.how: Connect Botany, Zoology, or Microbiology with its area of study.

rubric.why: Specialization lets researchers investigate a focused topic in depth.
rubric.how: Mention focused or detailed study and expertise.

rubric.why: Effective research depends on suitable methods and communication across fields.
rubric.description: Explain the wider benefit to research.
rubric.how: Mention better methods, shared findings, or solving biological problems.

modelAnswer: Biology covers many kinds of organisms and processes, so classification into branches makes the subject organised and easier to study.
Botany focuses on plants, Zoology on animals, and Microbiology on microorganisms.
Specialization allows scientists to develop detailed knowledge and methods for a particular field.
Scientists can also share findings across branches to solve wider biological problems.

written.text: Q1.2. How can a scientist apply the scientific method to confirm an observation that a certain plant species grows more quickly in shady places than in direct sunlight?
written.finalAnswer: The scientist should observe and record the difference, propose a testable hypothesis, and predict that plants of the species grown in shade will grow more quickly. The scientist should grow comparable plants in shade and direct sunlight while controlling other conditions, measure their growth regularly, repeat the experiment, and analyse the data. The results will show whether the hypothesis is supported, rejected, or needs modification.

rubric.why: A scientific investigation starts by recording the observation clearly.
rubric.how: Record the plant growth pattern and identify the question.

rubric.why: A testable hypothesis gives a proposed explanation or prediction.
rubric.how: Predict that the plants in shade grow more quickly.

rubric.why: A fair comparison requires two conditions and control of other factors.
rubric.how: Compare similar plants in shade and direct sunlight while keeping other conditions alike.

rubric.why: Measurements and analysis determine whether evidence supports the hypothesis.
rubric.description: Explain how to evaluate the experiment.
rubric.how: Measure growth, repeat the test, and analyse results against the hypothesis.

modelAnswer: Observe and record the growth pattern, and identify the question to be investigated.
Form the hypothesis: plants of this species grow more quickly in shady places than in direct sunlight.
Grow comparable plants in shade and direct sunlight, keeping other conditions such as water, soil, and plant age the same.
Measure and record their growth regularly, repeat the experiment, and analyse the results.
Use the evidence to decide whether the hypothesis is supported, rejected, or should be modified.

examTips: Section A tests branch names, definitions, and the order of the scientific-method steps; learn exact terms such as Cytology, Genetics, Taxonomy, and Embryology.
For short questions, give a direct definition or a clear two-part difference rather than a long unrelated explanation.
For a long question on the scientific method, write the steps in order: observations, hypothesis, deductions, experiments, and analysis of results.
For questions on malaria, state which scientist contributed each finding and make clear how the mosquito was linked with transmission.
For comparison questions, give both sides of the comparison, preferably in paired statements or a two-column table.
Marks are earned for correct scientific terms, ordered steps, relevant examples, and a conclusion supported by the evidence.

explain.title: Biology has many branches
explain.body: Biology covers many kinds of living organisms and processes. Branches such as Botany, Zoology, and Microbiology make the subject easier to organise and study. Other branches focus on a particular feature, such as cells, tissues, functions, development, or classification.

explain.title: Branches focus on different questions
explain.body: Genetics studies heredity and variation; Anatomy studies structure; and Physiology studies functions. Morphology is concerned with form and external features. Taxonomy deals with classification, while Embryology studies development from fertilization.

explain.title: Biology connects with other subjects
explain.body: Biology works with Physics, Chemistry, Statistics, Geography, Economics, and Computer Science. For example, Biochemistry studies chemical processes in living organisms, while Computational Biology uses computers to work with biological data.

explain.title: Scientific investigation follows ordered steps
explain.body: A scientist begins with observations, proposes a hypothesis, makes deductions, and tests them with experiments. Results are then analysed. Evidence may support a hypothesis, show that it should be rejected, or lead to its modification.

explain.title: Scientific knowledge is shared and tested
explain.body: Scientists share observations and results and build on earlier work. The investigation of malaria shows how different contributions about the parasite and mosquitoes helped explain how the disease spreads.

mistakes: Do not confuse Anatomy, which studies structure, with Physiology, which studies function.
Do not write that a hypothesis is always correct; it must be tested and can be rejected or modified.
Do not put experiments before deductions when giving the basic sequence used in this chapter.
Do not describe a branch only by its name; state what it studies.
In the malaria questions, do not say smoke kills parasites in the blood; the intended explanation is that smoke repels mosquitoes.
When describing an experiment, include what was changed, what was measured, and which other conditions were kept the same.
